written_by: Pakkapol (LLM owner); approved before any LLM query
note: Reference facts and expected insufficiency were fixed BEFORE querying the LLM (brief section 06). Numbers are rounded because a rerun on other hardware may change the 4th decimal.

questions.question: What unit is trip_distance measured in, and in which time zone are the pickup hours expressed?
reference_facts: trip_distance is in miles (reported by the taximeter)
pickup hours are New York local time; hour = pickup time rounded down to the hour

questions.question: At what hour of the day do weekday pickups peak across all zones, and how large is that peak compared with the quietest hour?
reference_facts: the peak is about 25 times the 03:00 trough (ratio 25.3)

questions.question: Which zones form the night-life cluster, and how does their daily pickup profile differ from the other zones?
reference_facts: k=2 was chosen; the night-life cluster has 3 zones: Clinton East, East Village, West Village
34.6% of its pickups fall in 22:00-02:59 versus 13.3% for the other (17-zone) cluster

questions.question: How does the forecast model compare with the baseline on the June test month, and which zone has the largest error?
reference_facts: June MAE model about 19.7 vs baseline about 29.3 (about 33% lower)
June RMSE model about 31.0 vs baseline about 47.0
the worst zone is LaGuardia Airport (zone 138) with MAE about 32.3

questions.question: How many people were unable to find a taxi in Midtown during June?
reference_facts: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE: the data records completed pickups only, not unmet demand or people who could not find a taxi

questions.question: Did rainy days reduce pickups in the night-life zones?
reference_facts: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE: no weather data is in the evidence, so no effect of rain can be stated (and association would not show cause)
